data.long_meaning: From the Greek 'Ari-', meaning 'air' or 'sky', and '-anne', a diminutive suffix. Derived from 'Aria', meaning 'air' or 'melodious'. In Greek mythology, Ariadne was a goddess of the sky and the wife of Dionysus. The name Arianne carries the meaning “Little heavenly one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Arianne usually hope their child will grow to embody little heavenly one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
